synopsis: Regression testing reruns previously passing cases after software or settings changes to detect newly broken required behaviour; the proposed campaign requires automatic regression on every change and makes captured, synthesised and search-discovered cases permanent tests [f14365, f6944, f7359, f1031, f14368]. Updates have materially changed field behaviour in on-road precedents, while changes to perception, sensors, mounting, braking or calibration can invalidate prior validation; every post-release software change therefore requires reassessment against accumulated safety evidence [f2013, f2940, f1156]. The proposed execution strategy combines smoke tests on every code change, mandatory safety tests on eligible builds, larger overnight or release-gate campaigns, and risk-selected hardware-in-the-loop and physical confirmation [f14369, f14370, f14371, f14372]. Within the four-month validation window, an existing automated pipeline is described as the only affordable way to check late tuning changes against earlier results, although demonstrating unchanged expected output remains a difficult simulation-tool integration task [f13531, f8723]. Regression volume does not establish operating-domain representativeness: the frozen estimation set must remain separate from continuous tuning, and late safety-relevant threshold changes require new independent statistical confirmation for affected claims [f14377, f14374, f14375].
